reason: The potato bay needs a lightproof skirt, and the foil and fabric look like suitable materials for one.
expectation: They will make a light-blocking cover for the potato bay.

effect: The foil-backed cloth blocks light and is ready to use as the potato bay’s skirt.
reaction: The lamp test makes its purpose clear.
reason: The prepared beds are where the potato bay needs its lightproof skirt.
expectation: The cloth will be fitted around the potato tuber space, leaving the shoots exposed to light.

effect: The potato bay is now shaded and ready for planting.
reaction: The distinction between shaded tubers and lit shoots is clear.
reason: The seed potatoes belong in the prepared dark potato bay.
expectation: The potatoes will be planted in the shaded bay.

effect: The potato bed is planted, leaving soybeans and lettuce to plant.
reaction: The deeper medium and dark skirt make the potato setup understandable.
reason: The soybean seeds belong in the prepared growing beds.
expectation: The soybeans will be planted in their designated row.

effect: The soybean row is sown, leaving the lettuce goal.
reaction: The spaced pockets and aerated row make the planting straightforward.
reason: The lettuce seeds belong in the remaining prepared tray.
expectation: The lettuce will be sown in its shallow tray.

effect: The lettuce seeds currently have no available combination, so the tray may need another preparation first.
reaction: That is surprising because the other seeds could be planted directly.
reason: Inspecting the prepared beds may reveal what remains to be done before planting lettuce.
expectation: The inspection will show available operations at the beds, possibly including a preparation for lettuce.

effect: Inspecting the beds automatically added a fabric wick, preparing the lettuce bed for planting.
reaction: The passive wick explains the extra preparation; it was not apparent from the initial board.
reason: The lettuce bed now has the wicking setup, so the seeds should be ready to plant.
expectation: The lettuce seeds will be sown in the prepared shallow bed.

effect: The lettuce is sown in the damp wick, completing all three planting goals.
reaction: The finished tray makes the wick’s role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the lettuce wick was most worthwhile: it showed how fabric can draw solution upward without another pump, a useful physical detail.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to plant lettuce directly was least worthwhile; the need for a wick was not apparent beforehand.

surprise.text: Lettuce could not be planted directly like the soybeans, and inspecting the beds automatically installed the missing wick.

arbitrary.text: The extra lettuce preparation initially felt arbitrary because the board did not indicate it was needed, though the wick’s function became clear afterward.

continue.text: I would continue: the practical growing-system details and the discovery of the wick made me curious about how the expedition develops.
